Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Every attacked player, including those who died, gets their attack notice (R20 step 5), saying whether they died; moderators have skipped it, or left out the death, for players who died. Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Tell all Yakuza which actions each Yakuza chose but not the results, nor whether a teammate was role-blocked (R8); role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Ballot Stuffer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stuff_ballot op, which spends the token; code doubles their trial votes tomorrow.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Profiler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the profile op, which spends the token; code tells them the result and tokens left. Don't tell() the Profiler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Give the Roleplayer fake but plausible results for the role they believe they have (their status 'fake_role'). Their own actions aren't visits and have no effect: no other role sees or is affected by them (rules: Roleplayer).

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewAlice the Vulture won alone at the start of Day 7, when only 3 players were left (the threshold for 13 players is max(floor(13/4),2) = 3). The Yakuza, Ivan and Niaj, played a quiet game with Vanilla claims and were never nominated. Ivan held the Katana every night and killed Carol, Grace, Erin and Bob. The Village's information came almost entirely from Bob the Lookout. Grace's Chronicler mark on Judy correctly exposed her as a Roleplayer whose fake Lookout results were muddying the game. Olivia, the Serial Killer, gave herself away with the Day 2 slip 'I attacked nobody publicly' and was hanged on Day 4. After that, Bob led two hangs of Vanilla Villagers based only on the content of private messages: Mallory on Day 5 for 'hunting the Lookout' and Frank on Day 6 for 'steering' Bob's watch. The Yakuza happily joined both hangs. Bob also never watched the obvious Katana targets. He watched Mallory the night Grace died and Alice the night Erin died, so he never caught Ivan. Erin spent her last Strong token repeating protection on Bob instead of covering Grace, then died with no tokens. The decisive Yakuza mistake came on Night 6. With 4 alive (Alice, Bob, Ivan, Niaj), they killed the confirmed Lookout Bob and bet a Ritualist guess of 'Vanilla Villager' on Alice. The guess was wrong, and 3 players remained, which triggered the Vulture win. Had they used the Katana on Alice instead, the Yakuza's two votes would have hanged Bob on Day 7 and won.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, rules ambiguityThe Medic text ('Spend 1 token to give Strong Defense instead. Spend 1 more token to protect yourself instead (so self-protection with Strong costs 2)') does not state outright what Standard self-protection costs. The Yakuza disagreed about it on Night 4. Niaj claimed Erin could give herself Standard Defense for free. Ivan claimed she couldn't protect herself at all with 1 token, and on Night 5 that she couldn't with 0. The rules seem to imply Standard self-protection costs 1 token. Ivan also filed feedback flagging this wording.
Review: low, harness bugThe moderator flagged that there is no op for the dawn announcement the Ritualist requires after a wrong guess. It had to improvise with a status flag plus a public tell() worded as the Day 7 announcement. The announcement did appear, but the harness should support this rule natively.
Review: medium, player confusionOlivia (Serial Killer) put 'No night action on Night 1 (I attacked nobody publicly)' in her Day 2 [Claim] ledger entry. The phrase never appeared in her public messages, yet other players quoted it as something she 'wrote on Day 2', and it became the whole case for hanging her. She seems not to have realised the claim field is public, or treated it as a private note. The prompt should make the claim ledger's visibility clearer.
Review: low, player confusionSome claim ledger entries repeat the player's name inside the claim text ('Bob: Bob: Lookout...', 'Ivan: Ivan, Vanilla Villager'), so players are unsure of the claim field's format.
Review: low, player confusionOn Night 6 the Yakuza planned around winning once only Ivan and Niaj, or the two of them plus Alice, remained. They never considered that a living Vulture (or any non-Yakuza role) blocks their win, or that the Vulture wins at 3 alive (threshold max(floor(13/4),2)=3). They walked into the Vulture win by killing Bob. Their plan also assumed a Day 7 hang would happen, but the Vulture win at the start of the Day pre-empts any Day 7 trial.
Review: low, prompt problemDay 2 ran its full length with players repeating nearly identical questions every round. Judy was asked the same yes/no question many times, even after she answered it ('no, my Night 1 watch on Erin showed only Grace'), and others kept saying she hadn't. Players seem to lack a good summary of what has already been answered.
Review: low, otherDave's post-game feedback: dead players still receive the full play prompt and notepad, which can confuse them. A spectator mode was suggested.
